topic: Love talk on the first reception shift
title_jp: はじめてのシフトで{恋|こい}バナ
context: Saturday: your first reception shift at Guesthouse Kaze, where you finally meet Kenta from Osaka. In the quiet hour after check-in he skips the small talk and goes straight to love, so you end up comparing dating in Japan and Spain.

phrases.jp: スペインと{比|くら|to compare}べて、{日本|にほん}の{恋愛|れんあい|romance, love life}ってどう？
phrases.en: Compared with Spain, what's dating like in Japan?
phrases.note: AとBを{比|くら}べると / Aと{比|くら}べて = compared with A. Polite: 〜と{比|くら}べて、どうですか。

phrases.jp: {告白|こくはく|confessing your feelings}されたこと、ある？
phrases.en: Has anyone ever confessed their feelings to you?
phrases.note: {告白|こくはく}する = tell someone you like them and ask them out. {告白|こくはく}される = be asked out (passive).

phrases.jp: {返事|へんじ|reply}は、なるべく{早|はや}く{返|かえ|to give back, reply}すようにしています。
phrases.en: I try to reply as soon as I can.
phrases.note: {返事|へんじ}を{返|かえ}す / {返信|へんしん}する = reply to a message. なるべく = as ~ as possible.

phrases.jp: {遠距離恋愛|えんきょりれんあい|long-distance relationship}って、{大変|たいへん}じゃない？
phrases.note: Everyone shortens it to {遠距離|えんきょり} or even {遠恋|えんれん}.

phrases.jp: {都会|とかい|big city}より{田舎|いなか|the countryside}のほうが{落|お}ち{着|つ|to feel calm, settle}く。
phrases.en: I feel more at ease in the countryside than in the city.
phrases.note: AよりBのほうが〜 = B is more ~ than A: the most common way to compare two things.

dialogue_setting: Guesthouse Kaze reception desk, Saturday afternoon, after the last hikers have checked in.

dialogue.speaker: Kenta
dialogue.jp: アルバートやんな？{俺|おれ}、{健太|けんた}。よろしゅう！で、いきなりやけど、{恋人|こいびと|boyfriend or girlfriend, partner}おるん？
dialogue.en: You're Albert, right? I'm Kenta. Nice to meet you! So, straight to it: got a partner?
dialogue.note: Kansai-ben: やんな = だよね, よろしゅう = よろしく, やけど = だけど, おるん？ = いるの？

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: いきなり！？いないよ。ねえ、スペインと{比|くら|to compare}べて、{日本|にほん}ではどうやって{付き合|つきあ|to go out with, date}い{始|はじ}めるの？
dialogue.en: Straight away?! No, I don't. Hey, compared with Spain, how do people start going out in Japan?

dialogue.speaker: Kenta
dialogue.jp: {日本|にほん}はな、まず「{告白|こくはく|confessing your feelings}」すんねん。「{好|す}きです、{付き合|つきあ|to go out with, date}ってください」って。そこから{恋人|こいびと|partner}になるんや。
dialogue.en: In Japan, first you do a 'kokuhaku'. 'I like you, please go out with me.' From that moment you're a couple.
dialogue.note: すんねん = するんだ, なるんや = なるんだ (Kansai). The standard version: まず{告白|こくはく}するんだ。

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: へえ。スペインは{告白|こくはく|confessing your feelings}より、{何回|なんかい}か{会|あ}って{自然|しぜん|naturally}に{付き合|つきあ}うことが{多|おお}いかな。メッセージの{返事|へんじ|reply}が{遅|おそ}くても、あんまり{気|き}にしないし。
dialogue.en: Huh. In Spain it's less about confessing: you meet a few times and it just happens. And nobody worries much if a reply to a message is slow.

dialogue.speaker: Kenta
dialogue.jp: そこはめっちゃ{違|ちが}うな。{俺|おれ}の{彼女|かのじょ}、{長野市|ながのし}で{看護師|かんごし|nurse}やねん。{遠距離|えんきょり|long distance}ってほどやないけど、{会|あ}えへん{分|ぶん|to make up for}、{毎晩|まいばん}{電話|でんわ}するようにしてんねん。
dialogue.en: That's a big difference. My girlfriend's a nurse in Nagano city. It's not exactly long-distance, but since we can't meet, I make a point of calling every night.
dialogue.note: めっちゃ = とても, やねん = なんだ, 〜ほどやない = 〜ほどじゃない (not as much as), {会|あ}えへん = {会|あ}えない, してんねん = しているんだ.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: えらいね。{僕|ぼく}も{家族|かぞく}に、{週|しゅう}に{一回|いっかい}は{連絡|れんらく|getting in touch}するようにしてる。でも{田舎|いなか|the countryside}って、{都会|とかい|big city}ほど{出会|であ|chance to meet people}いがなさそうだね。
dialogue.en: Good for you. I make sure to contact my family at least once a week too. But it looks like the countryside doesn't have as many chances to meet people as the city.

grammar.meaning: make an effort to, make a habit of
grammar.form: {動詞|どうし}{辞書形|じしょけい} + ようにする ({毎晩|まいばん}{電話|でんわ}するようにする) · {動詞|どうし}ない{形|けい} + ようにする ({遅|おく}れないようにする)
grammar.explanation: Use it for something you consciously try to do, or try not to do, again and again. 〜ようにしている describes a habit you already keep up; 〜ようにする is a resolution from now on. Don't mix it up with 〜ことにする (a one-off decision) or 〜ようになる (a change that happens to you, like becoming able to read kanji).

examples.jp: {毎日|まいにち}{少|すこ}しでも{日本語|にほんご}で{話|はな}すようにしています。
examples.en: I try to speak Japanese every day, even just a little.

examples.jp: {夜|よる}は{甘|あま}いものを{食|た}べないようにしてる。
examples.en: I make a point of not eating sweets at night.

examples.jp: {明日|あした}から、{朝|あさ}5{時|じ}に{起|お}きるようにします。
examples.en: From tomorrow I'll make sure to get up at 5.

quiz.question: {健康|けんこう|health}のために、{毎朝|まいあさ}{野菜|やさい}を＿＿ようにしている。
quiz.en: For my health, I make a habit of eating vegetables every morning.
quiz.explain: ようにする / ようにしている comes after the dictionary form (or the ない form): {食|た}べるようにしている.

kanji.meaning: matchmaking; tying the knot of fate
kanji.where: Written on charms (お守り) and wooden prayer plaques at shrines, and on posters for shrines famous for finding you a partner.
kanji.related: {縁結|えんむす}びのお{守|まも}り = a charm for finding love.
kanji.breakdown: {縁結|えんむす}び: 縁 bond, fate + 結び tying → 'tying people's fates together'.

tip.title: Why the 'kokuhaku' matters
tip.body: In Japan a relationship usually starts with a clear {告白|こくはく|confessing your feelings}: before it you're just people going out to eat; after it you're officially a couple. Couples often count the days from that moment and celebrate {付き合|つきあ}って1か{月|げつ} or 3か{月|げつ}. Coming from Spain, where things just drift into a relationship, it's worth asking yourself what the other person thinks you are.

challenge.prompt: Kenta grins: 「せやったら、アプリでも{入|い}れてみたら？こっちはみんな{使|つこ}うてるで。」 (= それなら、アプリでも入れてみたら？こっちはみんな使ってるよ。) Say you'll try it, but you'll make a point of meeting people in a café at first. Use 〜ようにする.
challenge.hint: {入|い}れてみる · {最初|さいしょ}は · カフェで{会|あ}う
challenge.model_answer: じゃあ、{入|い}れてみる！でも、{最初|さいしょ}はカフェで{会|あ}うようにするよ。
challenge.explanation: {入|い}れてみる = I'll try installing it (〜てみる = try and see). {会|あ}うようにする is a resolution from now on: dictionary form + ようにする. Casual speech fits a coworker your age; よ softens it into reassurance.

vocab.note: Gender-neutral. In speech people often say {彼氏|かれし} / {彼女|かのじょ} instead.

vocab.en: to go out with, date; to keep someone company
vocab.note: {付き合|つきあ}ってください = Please go out with me. Also: {買|か}い{物|もの}に{付き合|つきあ}う = come shopping with someone.

vocab.en: confessing your feelings, asking someone out

vocab.note: {連絡|れんらく}するね = I'll get in touch / message you.
{出会|であ}いがない = 'no chance to meet anyone', the classic complaint.

vocab.jp: {遠距離恋愛|えんきょりれんあい}
